1995.kid: The internet company’s modem bank: a rack with one little modem for every caller online right now. It answers your call, checks your password, gives your computer an address and sends your parcels on.
1995.nerd: A remote access server: dozens of digital modems on ISDN PRI lines from the exchange (V.34, 28.8 kbit/s). It terminates the PPP session, authenticates you against RADIUS, assigns an address from its pool and routes your packets onto the ISP’s LAN.
